draft.change: Append Genesis 10:18 to the evidence for definite-object in word 0.
draft.definition: Introduces the particular person or thing a verb acts on, ordinarily a definite noun identified by the article, a name or a possessive suffix.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 10:18 the first וְאֶת marks הָאַרְוָדִי as another object of יָלַד in Genesis 10:15.

analysis.evidence: The list governed by יָלַד in Genesis 10:15 continues with וְאֶת הָאַרְוָדִי, “and the Arvadite.” The article הָ־ makes the gentilic definite. The list ends before וְאַחַר נָפֹצוּ introduces the next clause.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins the next descendant to the list. The unsuffixed direct-object particle אֶת introduces הָאַרְוָדִי.
analysis.sense: Marks the Arvadite as a definite direct object of יָלַד, “fathered.”

draft.change: Add a noun entry for the gentilic אַרְוָדִי. Its form derives from the place name אַרְוָד, and its use in the clan list supports the gloss “Arvadites.”
draft.definition: A member of the people of Arvad, or the people collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:18 uses the definite singular for the Arvadites in its list of Canaanite clans.

analysis.evidence: The repeated וְאֶת places הָאַרְוָדִי alongside the Zemarites and Hamathites in Canaan’s genealogy. The closing phrase מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי identifies these groups as Canaanite clans.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular gentilic noun in the absolute state. The ending ־ִי marks affiliation with Arvad. The singular names the people collectively.
analysis.sense: The people of Arvad, counted among the Canaanite clans.

draft.change: Add the gentilic צְמָרִי with its collective use in the genealogy of Canaan.
draft.definition: A Zemarite, a member of one of the Canaanite clans.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:18 names the Zemarites among the Canaanite families and uses a singular gentilic for the group.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:18 lists הַצְּמָרִי between the Arvadite and the Hamathite, introducing each with וְאֶת. The closing phrase מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי, “the families of the Canaanite,” identifies the groups just listed.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial צ of the masculine singular absolute gentilic noun צְמָרִי. The singular designates the clan collectively.
analysis.sense: A member of the Zemarite clan, here denoting the clan as a whole.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew gentilic חֲמָתִי derived from the place name חֲמָת.
draft.definition: A member of the people of Hamath.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:18 lists the Hamathites among the Canaanite families.

analysis.evidence: The repeated וְאֶת places הַחֲמָתִי alongside the Arvadite and the Zemarite. The following clause calls these groups מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי, “the families of the Canaanite,” establishing the collective reading.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular gentilic noun in the absolute state. The ending ־ִי forms the gentilic from חֲמָת, Hamath. The singular denotes the people collectively.
analysis.sense: A member of the people of Hamath, here denoting the clan collectively.

analysis.evidence: אַחַר modifies the verb נָפֹצוּ and takes no complement. After the list of Canaanite peoples, the clause states that the Canaanite clans subsequently dispersed.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ prefixes the temporal adverb אַחַר.

analysis.evidence: וְאַחַר means “and afterward.” The subject מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי identifies the Canaanite clans as those who spread out. The verse names no agent or host peoples among whom the clans were scattered.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, third person common plural, agreeing with the plural subject מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי.

analysis.evidence: מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי means “the families of the Canaanites.” These families are the plural subject of נָפֹצוּ, “they dispersed.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine plural common noun in the construct state, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי, “the clans of the Canaanites,” the gentilic identifies the people to whom the clans belong. The preceding list names clans individually, including the Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute gentilic used substantivally. The singular refers collectively to the Canaanites.
